nodes.name: NF cleaning
nodes.procedure: NF (2.5 cm × 3.5 cm × 1.5 mm) was initially subjected to ultrasonic cleaning in acetone, hydrochloric acid (1 M), and ethanol, each for 15 min. Thorough removal of oxides and organic residues from the NF surfaces played a crucial role in the preparation of the electrocatalysts for this study.
nodes.source_text: NF (2.5 cm * 3.5 cm * 1.5 mm) was initially subjected to ultrasonic cleaning in acetone, hydrochloric acid (1 M), and ethanol, each for 15 min. Thorough removal of oxides and organic residues from the NF surfaces played a crucial role...

nodes.name: NiFe-SQ/NF hydrothermal synthesis
nodes.procedure: The cleaned NF was placed in a solution comprising 0.3000 g of PVP, 2.5 mmol of squaric acid, 0.5 mmol of Fe(NO3)3·9H2O, and 30 ml of deionized water. Then, the mixture was transferred to a 100 mL Teflon vessel sealed with a stainless autoclave, heated to 120°C, and maintained for 6 h. The resulting dark green NiFe-SQ/NF sample was obtained after rinsing with deionized water and drying in a vacuum oven at 60°C.

nodes.name: NiFe-SQ/NF-R electrochemical activation
nodes.procedure: NiFe-SQ/NF underwent electrochemical activation in 1 M KOH. The specific activation process involved cyclic voltammetry in a standard three-electrode configuration, with a scanning range of 0−1.488 V versus RHE, a scanning rate of 10 mV s−1, and a total of 10 cycles.

nodes.name: NiFe-LDH/NF hydrothermal synthesis
nodes.procedure: The process of synthesizing NiFe-LDH/NF-R closely mirrors that of NiFe-SQ/NF-R, differing primarily in replacing the solution with 1.0 mmol of Ni(NO3)2·6H2O, 0.5 mmol of Fe(NO3)3·9H2O, 2.5 mmol of NH4F, 6 mmol of CO(NH2)2, and 30 ml of deionized water.

nodes.characterization_summary: NiFe-SQ/NF exhibits a distinct cuboid angular stack structure growing uniformly on NF surface.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in Fig. 1b, NiFe-SQ/NF exhibited a distinct cuboid angular stack structure, growing uniformly and closely on the initially smooth NF surface.

nodes.characterization_summary: Fe, Ni, O and C elements are uniformly distributed on the surface of NiFe-SQ/NF.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The scanning electron microscopy (SEM)-mapping images show that Fe, Ni, O and C elements are uniformly distributed on the surface of NiFe-SQ/NF.

nodes.characterization_summary: The ratio of iron to nickel in the NiFe-SQ/NF sample was approximately 0.39.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The analysis conducted using inductively coupled plasma-optical emission spectroscopy (ICP-OES) revealed that the ratio of iron to nickel in the NiFe-SQ/NF sample was approximately 0.39.

nodes.characterization_summary: NiFe-SQ/NF reveals distinctive peaks associated with the Ni-Fe coordination polymer and metallic Ni.
nodes.evidence_snippet: X-ray diffraction (XRD) analysis of NiFe-SQ/NF reveals distinctive peaks associated with the Ni-Fe coordination polymer and metallic Ni.

nodes.characterization_summary: Only the peaks of metal Ni were detected in the XRD pattern of NiFe-SQ/NF-R.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Only the peaks of metal Ni were detected in the XRD pattern of NiFe-SQ/NF-R.

nodes.characterization_summary: NiFe-SQ/NF-R shows net-like fissure structure due to alkaline hydrolysis during activation.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Alkaline hydrolysis occurs on the surface of NiFe-SQ/NF during electrochemical anodic activation treatment, causing some Sq2− to run off and creating a net-like fissure structure in NiFe-SQ/NF-R.

nodes.characterization_summary: Short and disordered lattice fringes in the outer reconstructed layer of NiFe-SQ/NF-R attributed to metallic hydroxyl oxides.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Specifically, in Fig. 1d, short and disordered lattice fringes can be observed in the outer reconstructed layer of NiFe-SQ/NF-R, which are attributed to metallic hydroxyl oxides.

nodes.characterization_summary: Selected-area electron diffraction pattern of NiFe-SQ/NF-R matches r-NiOOH (PDF# 00-006-0075).
nodes.evidence_snippet: The selected-area electron diffraction pattern (Supplementary Fig. 12) for NiFe-SQ/NF-R exhibits similar structural information that matches that of r-NiOOH.

nodes.characterization_summary: NiFe-SQ/NF-R shows (105) crystal face of NiOOH at 0.210 nm due to Sq2− intercalation.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The presence of Sq2− insertion leads to a noticeable broadening of the (105) crystal face of NiOOH, measuring at 0.210 nm.

nodes.characterization_summary: Elemental mappings show homogeneous distribution of Ni, Fe, O, and C in NiFe-SQ/NF-R.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The element mapping images of NiFe-SQ/NF-R under high-resolution AC-TEM reveal a homogeneous distribution of Ni, Fe, O, and C.

nodes.characterization_summary: Slight shift in Ni2+ 2p3/2 and Ni3+ 2p3/2 peaks for NiFe-SQ/NF-R vs NiFe-LDH/NF-R; discernible distinctions in Fe sites environment.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The results depicted in Fig. 3a illustrate a slight shift in the Ni2+ 2p3/2 and Ni3+ 2p3/2 peaks between NiFe-SQ/NF-R and NiFe-LDH/NF-R, implying a closely resembling electronic configuration surrounding the Ni sites in both. Nonetheless, discernible distinctions were observed in the Fe sites environment between the two.

nodes.characterization_summary: Electrolyte after CV activation of NiFe-SQ/NF shows Raman characteristic peaks attributed to Sq2− matching KOH solution of Sq2−.
nodes.evidence_snippet: To illustrate this phenomenon, a comparison was conducted between the electrolyte after CV activation and the KOH solution of Sq2−, revealing that they have similar Raman characteristic peaks attributed to Sq2−.

nodes.characterization_summary: NiFe-LDH/NF-R exhibits longer-range ordered distribution of the (101) crystal plane.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Under the same test conditions, NiFe-LDH/NF-R exhibits a longer-range ordered distribution of the (101) crystal plane.

nodes.characterization_summary: NiFe-LDH/NF transforms from Ni(OH)2 (455, 530 cm−1) to (Fe-doped) NiOOH (475, 550 cm−1) under oxidation current.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The in situ Raman analysis revealed that the NiFe-LDH/NF experienced a reconstruction process under the excitation of oxidation current, leading to the gradual transformation of Ni(OH)2 (455, 530 cm−1) into (Fe-doped) NiOOH (475, 550 cm−1).

nodes.characterization_summary: Unintercalated NiOOH shows (105) crystal face at 0.205 nm compared to standard 0.209 nm.
nodes.evidence_snippet: However, our actually observations show that the (105) crystal face of unintercalated NiOOH produced by electrochemical activation is slightly smaller at 0.205 nm under identical test conditions.
